comment: Single source of truth for the accuracy bands. Edit this file and run
python make_bands.py
to regenerate every mnist-medium-<band>/task.yml and sutro.yaml.
error_bp is the maximum MEAN error in basis points over all draws of a
ranked run: the aggregate rule is
sum(correct) >= ceil(draws * test * (10000 - error_bp) / 10000).
draw_slack_bp adds a per-draw floor on top of it, so a submission cannot
buy the mean by running a cheap learner on some of the draws.
A 15% entry band is { name: mnist-medium-15pct, error_bp: 1500 } and the
1.6% top band under discussion is { name: mnist-medium-1p6pct,
error_bp: 160 }; add either as one more object in bands[] and rerun.
holdout_draws Fashion-MNIST calls are interleaved with the ranked ones at
secret positions; they are timed and ranked like any other call and must
clear holdout_min_bp in aggregate. 3000 bp (70%) was calibrated on the
harness 1.1.1 PIXEL release, on an A100: pca_qda 78.0%, the
conjugate-gradient pair 88.2%, mlp512 47.8% (which fails, and is an honest
learner; see the residual risks in README.md). Those three numbers are not
re-measured under release_dims 60 on a GPU; on CPU released Fashion draws
(10,000/10,000, two hold-out draws) pca_qda scores 75.4% and ncm_baseline
77.6%, so the margin over the floor is a few points and closing. Re-measure
before changing this number.
release_dims is the width of the linear release z = Q W (x - mu) that a
draw hands over instead of pixels: exact PCA whitening onto that many
principal directions of the draw's own training rows, then a secret
per-draw Haar rotation. 60 of 81 keeps essentially all the signal (an
honest dense learner loses under a point) while deleting the pixel
lattice and the pixel covariance. 0 releases the raw 9x9 pixels, which is
what harness 1.1.1 did.
Anything else a band may vary lives in defaults/ below and can be
overridden per band with the same keys.
